summary: Iran peace negotiations remain the dominant macro force, with Trump declaring talks in their "final stages" — progress that has pulled oil back from near $110 and eased inflation pressure at the margin. But the oil shock has already rekindled inflation fears and driven a growing consensus that the Fed will not cut rates this year, with traders now pricing in a rate hike as more likely.
tweet: Iran deal progress pulled oil off its highs, but FOMC minutes flagging possible hikes and a 40% December hike probability keep real rates elevated — stocks greed, gold and bonds squeezed.
